body: Buy Blue Books and calculator batteries at the beginning of the semester so you’re prepared and calm on test days.
Don’t forget to get enough sleep before tests. Fatigue leads to poor focus and memory.
Get ready for test breaks by buying healthy snacks such as dry fruits and nuts.
Alternate study with brief exercise periods. Even running up and down stairs helps break the study stress.
Review past tests to identify items you did and didn’t do correctly. Discuss patterns with instructor or tutor.
Wake up early so that you do not need to rush through having breakfast and getting ready.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Check the venue and time of the exam to make sure that you have not confused the day/time/venue.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Have a balanced breakfast and eat nothing risky (probably not the best day to have a super-hot curry!). Bananas are always a good option.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Before leaving home, check that you have everything that you will need – ID, stationery, map to the exam venue, etc.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Head to the exam with plenty of time. A lot of unexpected events can happen on your way there and you do not want to be late!
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: If there are people around who are panicking, avoid them. They are not doing you any favour!
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Go to the toilet before the exam starts. Exams can be quite long and there is no time to waste.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Remember to write your name on the exam paper. You would not believe how many people have forgotten to do it!
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Read all the questions carefully before starting and quickly plan how much time to allocate to each.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Start answering the questions that you feel most confident about. There is no need to answer the questions in order.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: If your brain freezes, just start writing anything and you will soon start remembering more details.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Don’t spend more time than you planned on a particular section/question or you might run out of time to answer other questions and gain those extra marks! Also,  leave any questions that you are unsure about for the end.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Don’t be afraid to ask the examiner if you are not clear on a question.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Use every minute of the exam and if you have time left, review your answers before handing back the paper.
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Stay calm, you have done your homework and have nothing to fear!
category: Success on the Exam Day Tips

body: Preview the text before the lecture. Write or diagram a summary. Develop questions to answer during the lecture.
Prepare your note taking paper by writing questions that you think might be addressed during the lecture.
Ask permission to stand up if you can’t sit and focus for a long lecture. Say,“When I stand, I won’t disturb anyone.”
Sit close to the speaker to stay involved and attentive, this helps you hear the information accurately and avoid distraction.
Do not assume that because you have hand outs or PowerPoint slides, you don’t need to take lecture notes or review.
Add contextual comments or sketch doodles in your notes to emphasize facts, reflect attitudes, or illustrate new terms.
Audio record lectures in difficult courses; note the counter number on the bottom of the page for easy access and review.
Record the number of each PowerPoint slide in your notes for easy access and review.
Take mini breaks of 1 to 2 minutes during a lecture to maintain focus and concentration. Take a few deep breaths and stretch.
Focus on the definitions of key terms and concentrate on learning a few facts during the lecture.
Write a summary of main ideas at the end of each lecture, and then add a few facts and examples.
Draw a diagram, chart, map or timeline to summarize information presented in the lecture.
Use the lecture notes as a guide to the most important aspects of the course, learning the main ideas, facts, and examples.
Study a little each day and review the previous day’s lecture before beginning a new topic.
Review and edit your notes within 24 to 48 hours of the lecture. This enhances comprehension and memory.
Don’t read and reread your notes. Identify important points, repeat and write the information in your own words.
Use color–coded sticky notes to remember vocabulary, main ideas or examples when you review notes.
Enlarge slides that illustrate complicated material so they are easier to read and learn in segments.
Edit your notes by referring to texts and other reading, then, consolidate information by creating charts or diagrams.
Relate and integrate the information from lectures and discussions to textbook and supplemental reading; why is it important?
Listen to a podcast of a lecture while walking or exercising. Write key ideas or facts when you stop the activity.
Test your retention of lecture material by visualizing graphics, reciting main ideas and then writing notes from memory.
Use lecture notes to identify questions that you can ask in discussions or address during office hours.
Convert the title of each lecture into one or more questions. Use these questions to generate topics for papers.
Use your lecture notes to create short–answer and multiple–choice questions. Use these to locate details and prepare for tests.
Take time to relax before you read; stretch and take a few deep breathes, then energize by visualizing a past success.
View reading as a method of processing information rather than a mechanical act of reading each word.
Create a mental image about the information you read. Remember that one picture is worth a thousand words.
Take frequent, brief breaks to relax. Read for 25 minutes; take a 5–minute break. Take four deep breaths and a few stretches.
Summarize out loud the main ideas that you learn. Schedule 3 to 5 minutes for every 30 minutes you study.
